class.name: NetwPredictJournal
class.brief_description: Packed-column snapshot of the transitions a prediction engine drove.
class.description: Production ownership stays in the native engine. A caller never builds one up: [method NetwPredictionHandle.journal] materializes this tooling-cadence view without changing the retained native rows, and [code skip-lint]NetwPredictJournal.new()[/code] itself yields an empty snapshot with [method size] zero. A closed row names one drive completely. A row is a complete account of the transition it names, so a transition is reproducible from its row alone. Nothing the engine decided is held outside the row and read back later, which is what lets two peers compare transitions instead of comparing engines. Two peers that ran the same transition closure agree on [method post_fps] at every acked transition, and the first transition where they disagree is the one that broke, not the one where the error grew visible. A native enum is not a [Dictionary] at runtime the way a GDScript enum is, so [method attribution_names], [method operator_names], [method domain_names], and [method state_family_names] exist for a caller that wants a name for a stored value rather than the bare [enum Attribution], [enum Operator], [enum Domain], or [enum StateFamily]. [codeblock] var journal := entity.prediction.journal() var transitions := journal.transitions() var flags := journal.flags() for i in transitions.size(): if flags[i] & NetwPredictJournal.ROW_DIVERGENT: print("diverged at transition ", transitions[i]) break [/codeblock]

method.name: attribution_at
method.description: Returns the [enum Attribution] charged to [param transition], or [constant Attribution.UNKNOWN] when nothing charged it or the row has fallen out of the ring.

method.name: attribution_names
method.description: Returns [enum Attribution] member names mapped to their values, for looking a value up by name where a bare enum offers no such lookup.

method.name: attributions
method.description: Returns the retained divergence charges, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: c_hashes
method.description: Returns the retained command fingerprints, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: capacity
method.description: Returns how many rows the journal retains before the oldest falls off.

method.name: clear
method.description: Drops every retained row and adopts [param epoch]. Transitions are injective only within one epoch, so a journal that outlives an epoch would hold two rows claiming the same transition. Clearing is how a rewire keeps [method row_at] unambiguous.

method.name: domain_at
method.description: Returns the [enum Domain] recorded for [param transition], or [constant Domain.OUT_OF_DOMAIN] when the row has fallen out of the ring. A transition nobody retained is one nobody can show was entitled to exactness, so the forgotten row reads as the label that claims nothing.

method.name: domain_names
method.description: Returns [enum Domain] member names mapped to their values, for looking a value up by name where a bare enum offers no such lookup.

method.name: domains
method.description: Returns the retained [enum Domain] values, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: e_digests
method.description: Returns the retained environment digests, ordered by [method transitions]. A row whose engine declares no environment facts carries [code]0[/code].

method.name: epoch
method.description: Returns the epoch [method clear] last adopted, or [code]-1[/code] before any.

method.name: evidence_masks
method.description: Returns the retained evidence-completeness masks, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: first_chain_break
method.description: Returns the first retained transition marked [constant ROW_CHAIN_BROKEN], or [code]-1[/code] when the retained chain is intact.

method.name: first_unmatched
method.description: Returns the oldest transition whose row is not [constant ROW_MATCHED], or [code]-1[/code] when every retained row matched. This is the transition a recovery rebases at.

method.name: flags
method.description: Returns the retained [code]ROW_[/code] bitfields, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: flags_at
method.description: Returns the [code]ROW_*[/code] bitfield recorded for [param transition], or [code]0[/code] when the row has fallen out of the ring. This and [method domain_at] are the per-transition reads the compare path makes on every authoritative frame, which is why they return a scalar instead of going through [method row_at]. Materializing a row dictionary to read one byte out of it allocates once per frame per predicted entity.

method.name: fnv1a
method.description: Returns the fingerprint of [param bytes] as fnv1a-32, the one hash the journal, the wire, and every later comparison share. The result is a signed 32-bit integer because that is the width the columns and the wire both carry, so a fingerprint never changes representation between being computed, stored, and sent.

method.name: kinds
method.description: Returns the retained [enum NetwPredict.DriveKind] values, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: labels
method.description: Returns the retained clock labels, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: last_closed
method.description: Returns the newest transition whose row is [constant ROW_CLOSED] with every older retained row closed too, or [code]-1[/code] when none is. This is the frontier an acknowledgement may claim. A row that is open holds a zero fingerprint, so acknowledging it would assert a state the drive has not produced yet.

method.name: operator_names
method.description: Returns [enum Operator] member names mapped to their values, for looking a value up by name where a bare enum offers no such lookup.

method.name: post_family_fps
method.description: Returns [param family]'s retained post-state fingerprint column, ordered by [method transitions]. An open row carries [code]0[/code] until the drive closes.

method.name: post_fps
method.description: Returns the retained post-solve state fingerprints, ordered by [method transitions]. An open row carries [code]0[/code] until the drive closes.

method.name: pre_family_fps
method.description: Returns [param family]'s retained pre-state fingerprint column, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: pre_fps
method.description: Returns the retained pre-state fingerprints, ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: raw_fps
method.description: Returns the retained raw pre-state fingerprints, ordered by [method transitions]. A row without [constant EVIDENCE_RAW] carries zero.

method.name: row_at
method.description: Returns the row recorded for [param transition], or an empty [Dictionary] when it has fallen out of the ring. This is the tooling-cadence read. Bulk readers take the columns through [method transitions] and its siblings instead of materializing a row per transition. [codeblock lang=text] Dictionary ┠╴transition int the recurrence index, injective within an epoch ┠╴label int the clock label the drive carried ┠╴kind int a DriveKind value naming the command selection ┠╴c_hash int fingerprint of the canonical command bytes ┠╴e_digest int fingerprint of the declared environment facts ┠╴post_fp int fingerprint of the state the drive produced ┠╴domain int a Domain value ┠╴attribution int an Attribution value ┖╴flags int the ROW_ bitfield [/codeblock] The row also exposes [code]pre_fp[/code], the pre and post [code]pose_fp[/code], [code]momentum_fp[/code], and [code]controller_fp[/code] families, plus the preceding operator's [code]episode_id[/code], [code]write_id[/code], [code]operator[/code], and [code]basis[/code]. Settled rows expose [code]aligned_error[/code], and witnessed rows expose [code skip-lint]witness_class_bits[/code].

method.name: size
method.description: Returns how many rows the journal currently retains, at most [method capacity].

method.name: state_family_names
method.description: Returns [enum StateFamily] member names mapped to their values, for looking a value up by name where a bare enum offers no such lookup.

method.name: topo_fps
method.description: Returns the retained execution-topology fingerprints, ordered by [method transitions]. The declared quantum is folded into this hash, and nothing else is. The quantum is how many physics steps a drive actually bought, and it belongs here because the physics server integrates on its own cadence: a drive and a solve are two events, and only their ratio makes a compared transition mean the same thing on both peers. Without it the boundary ladder walks all the way to closure and reports that every antecedent agreed. A different quantum is therefore a different topology, deliberately, and two peers running the same commands at different cadences disagree here rather than nowhere.

method.name: transitions
method.description: Returns the retained transitions oldest first. Every other column accessor returns values in this same order, so index [code]i[/code] names one row across all of them.

method.name: witness_class_bits
method.description: Returns authority witness-class summaries ordered by [method transitions].

method.name: witness_fps
method.description: Returns the retained realized-witness fingerprints, ordered by [method transitions]. A row without [constant EVIDENCE_WITNESS] carries zero.

constants.constant: How many transitions a journal retains before the oldest row falls off when none is given explicitly.
The row has been acknowledged by authority. Set by [code]mark_ack[/code] on the native engine.
The acknowledged authority state fingerprinted equal to [method post_fps].
Authority ran a command the owner never authored for this transition.
A later acknowledgement replaced this row's verdict with a truer one.
The acknowledged authority state fingerprinted unequal to [method post_fps].
The row's drive has produced its state, so [method post_fps] carries a real fingerprint rather than the zero an open row holds.
The row's [method pre_fps] did not chain from the preceding produced state and no operator provenance accounts for the intervening write.
Both peers declared a realized witness for the row and its fingerprint matched. The local witness detail may therefore describe the peer's stable witness facts too.
The row carries a declared realized-transition witness.
The row carries the optional raw pre-state fingerprint.
Required peer evidence was absent, so no boundary is blamed.
The peers entered the transition with different declared state.
The command differed. Authority ran input the owner did not author.
The environment differed. The transition ran against unequal world facts.
The execution topology or body mode differed.
Canonical state agreed but optional raw execution bits differed.
Equal observed antecedents produced a different contact witness.
Every observed antecedent agreed but the produced state differed.
No operator wrote the body since the preceding row.
A projected authoritative basis was restored.
An exact authoritative basis was restored.
The teleport tier restored the full declared closure.
Present-time moving transport composed an aligned delta.
Fallback seeded the body from authority.
The first post-reseed comparison aligned the acknowledgement horizon.
A witnessed boundary breach closed speculation without closing input.
A clean momentum-only divergence was left to contract without a write.
A joint pass restored the whole replay group to its shared floor.

No family differed or the peer evidence was unavailable. Named [code skip-lint]FAMILY_NONE[/code] rather than [code skip-lint]NONE[/code] because a bound enum's members flatten into the class namespace alongside [enum Operator], which already claims [code skip-lint]NONE[/code].
Position and orientation fields.
Declared derivative and velocity fields.
Remaining controller state and latches.
Every antecedent of the transition is declared equal on both peers, so its fingerprints must match exactly.
An antecedent is declared unequal or unknown, so the transition is compared by tolerance rather than by fingerprint.
